mainTopic: Wick laws, רב נתן בר אבא's sayings on compassion and dependence, and a new משנה on kitchen preparations and building on יום טוב
overview: The amud starts by asking why cutting a wick in two is forbidden on יום טוב, when cutting it with fire is allowed. רבי חייא explains that the fire method means lighting one long wick between two lamps. רב permits removing the burnt tip of a wick, and בר קפרא lists six wick rules: three strict and three lenient. Next comes a series of sayings by רב נתן בר אבא: the wealthy of Babylonia, who refused to help שבתאי בר מרינוס, lack the compassion that marks אברהם's children, and a person who depends on others' tables lives a dark life. A ברייתא then lists three people whose lives are 'not lives.' A new משנה lists kitchen actions forbidden on יום טוב: breaking clay or cutting paper for roasting, sweeping out an oven, setting up barrels or propping a pot, and leading an animal with a stick. The גמרא explains these rules. Sweeping is allowed when baking is impossible otherwise, and an oven may be sealed with ready-made riverbank mud or ashes. Bathroom stones may be arranged out of respect for human dignity. A bonfire may be stacked from the top down but not from the bottom up.

steps.title: Why is cutting a wick forbidden, if cutting with fire is allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the reason cutting a wick in two is forbidden is 'fixing a vessel', and then challenges this: cutting with fire also fixes a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it forbidden because he is fixing a vessel? But when he cuts it with fire, he is also fixing a vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is looking for the reason that cutting a wick in two is forbidden on יום טוב. It suggests 'fixing a vessel' and immediately attacks that reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Turning one wick into two usable wicks could count as making or fixing a usable item (מתקן מנא). But cutting the wick with fire is permitted, and that also ends with two usable wicks. So if fixing a vessel were the problem, the fire method should be forbidden too.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixing or preparing a vessel or usable item, which is forbidden work

phrases.english: Is it because he is fixing a vessel?
phrases.notes: The question starts just before this line: why is cutting the wick in two forbidden on יום טוב?

phrases.english: With fire too, he is fixing a vessel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the reason behind the ban on cutting a wick
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that cutting a wick is forbidden because of 'fixing a vessel'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Cutting with fire is allowed, yet it also produces two usable wicks. So 'fixing a vessel' cannot be the whole reason.

steps.title: The fire method means lighting one wick between two lamps
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא explains that the permitted fire method is to stretch one wick between two lamps and light it in the middle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא taught: He cuts it with fire at the mouth of two lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא answers the challenge by explaining what the permitted 'cutting with fire' really is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is not cutting a wick to make two wicks. He puts one long wick into two lamps and lights it, so the wick splits only because he is lighting the lamps. Since the 'fixing' is just a side effect of lighting, it is permitted, while plain cutting is still forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: At the mouth of two lamps

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya taught:
He cuts it with fire
at the mouth of two lamps.
phrases.notes: He puts one long wick into two lamps and lights it in the middle, so it splits only through the lighting.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַבִּי חִיָּיא חוֹתְכָהּ בָּאוּר בְּפִי שְׁתֵּי נֵרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cutting with fire is just another way of cutting a wick into two.
steps.terutzMaskana: Cutting with fire means lighting one wick between two lamps, so the split comes only from lighting.

steps.title: רב permits doing מוחטין to a wick on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר אבא quotes רב: one may do 'מוחטין' to a wick on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן בר אבא said in the name of רב: One may do 'מוחטין' to the wick on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling about wicks from רב. It uses an unclear word, which sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a leniency about handling a wick on יום טוב. The key word 'מוחטין' is not clear, so the גמרא will need to explain it.

keyTerms.meaning: Cleaning or trimming the wick (explained in the next steps)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Natan bar Abba said that Rav said:
One may 'mochet' the wick on Yom Tov.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling on the same topic of wicks
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may do מוחטין to a wick on יום טוב.

steps.title: What does מוחטין mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the word מוחטין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'מוחטין' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple word question. It wants to know what action רב permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. You cannot know what is allowed until you know what the word means.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What does 'mochatin' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks to explain the word in step 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word מוחטין

steps.title: מוחטין means removing the burnt part
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא בר שלמיא explains: it means removing the darkness, that is, the burnt tip of the wick.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא בר שלמיא said: It means removing the darkness.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the word question. מוחטין means clearing away the burnt, dark part of the wick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A burnt, charred tip makes the lamp dim. Removing it makes the light brighter, and רב allows this on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Darkness (here, the burnt black part of the wick)

phrases.english: Rav Chanina bar Shelemya said
(in the name of Rav):
phrases.notes: These words are in round brackets because some versions leave them out.

phrases.english: To remove the darkness.
phrases.notes: He means taking off the burnt, blackened tip of the wick so the flame burns brighter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מוחטין means removing the burnt, dark part of the wick.

steps.title: בר קפרא: six rules about a wick
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא introduces a list of six wick rules: three strict and three lenient.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא taught: Six things were said about a wick, three to be strict and three to be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching of בר קפרא. This line sets up the list that comes in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching collects all the main wick rules for יום טוב in one place. It sorts them into two groups so they are easy to remember.

phrases.english: Bar Kappara taught:
Six things were said about a wick.
Three to be strict, and three to be lenient.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי בַּר קַפָּרָא שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים נֶאֶמְרוּ בִּפְתִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another teaching on wicks
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are six wick rules on יום טוב: three strict and three lenient.

steps.title: The three strict rules
steps.stepSummary: One may not twist a wick from scratch, singe it in fire, or cut it in two.
steps.simpleTranslation: To be strict: One may not twist it from the start on יום טוב, one may not singe it in fire, and one may not cut it in two.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא lists the three things you may not do to a wick on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a new wick, singeing it to prepare it, and cutting it in two are all ways of making a ready-to-use item. The third rule is the same ban the גמרא discussed in step 1.

phrases.english: To be strict:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין גּוֹדְלִין אוֹתָהּ לְכַתְּחִלָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: One may not twist it from the start on Yom Tov,
and one may not singe it in fire,
and one may not cut it in two.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְהַחְמִיר אֵין גּוֹדְלִין אוֹתָהּ לְכַתְּחִלָּה בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first half of the list from step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may not twist a new wick, singe it, or cut it in two.

steps.title: The three lenient rules
steps.stepSummary: One may crush a wick by hand, soak it in oil, and split it with fire between two lamps.
steps.simpleTranslation: To be lenient: One may crush it by hand, soak it in oil, and cut it with fire at the mouth of two lamps.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא lists the three things you may do to a wick on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These actions help the wick burn without making a new item in the normal way. The last one is the same fire method רבי חייא explained in step 2.
steps.whatToRemember: Wick rules on יום טוב: no twisting, singeing, or cutting. But crushing by hand, soaking in oil, and splitting by lighting it between two lamps are allowed.

phrases.english: To be lenient:
one may crush it by hand,
and soak it in oil,
and cut it with fire at the mouth of two lamps.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the list from step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may crush a wick by hand, soak it in oil, and split it with fire between two lamps.

steps.title: The wealthy of Babylonia are headed for גיהנם
steps.stepSummary: Another saying of רב נתן בר אבא in the name of רב: the rich people of Babylonia go down to גיהנם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב נתן בר אבא said in the name of רב: The wealthy of Babylonia go down to גיהנם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It brings another saying by the same רב נתן בר אבא, this time about how people treat others.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link to the earlier steps is only that the same teacher said it. The next steps explain why רב said such a harsh thing.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Natan bar Abba said that Rav said:
The wealthy of Babylonia are ones who go down to Gehinnom.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same teacher as step 3, new topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wealthy of Babylonia are destined for גיהנם.

steps.title: The story of שבתאי בר מרינוס
steps.stepSummary: שבתאי בר מרינוס came to Babylonia and asked for a business partnership and then for food, and the rich refused both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the incident when שבתאי בר מרינוס came to Babylonia. He asked them for a business deal and they did not give it to him. He asked them to feed him, and they did not feed him either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows why רב spoke so harshly about the wealthy of Babylonia.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First he asked for a business partnership, which would have been fair for them too. Then he asked only for food, the most basic help. They refused both, which shows they had no compassion at all.

phrases.english: Like this incident, where Shabbetai bar Marinus
happened to come to Babylonia,
he asked them for a business deal —
and they did not give it to him.
To feed him food —
they also did not feed him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows by example the statement of step 9
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the wealthy of Babylonia lack compassion
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of שבתאי בר מרינוס

steps.title: These people come from the ערב רב
steps.stepSummary: שבתאי בר מרינוס says these rich people must come from the ערב רב, not from אברהם.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: These people come from the ערב רב.
steps.whatsHappening: שבתאי reacts to how he was treated. He says these people must come from the ערב רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He is saying that people with no compassion cannot really be אברהם's children. The next step brings the פסוק that supports this.

keyTerms.meaning: The mixed crowd that left Egypt together with the Jews

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר: הָנֵי מֵעֵרֶב רַב קָא אָתוּ,
phrases.english: He said: These people come from the mixed multitude,
phrases.notes: The ערב רב were non-Jews who joined the Jews when they left Egypt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר הָנֵי מֵעֵרֶב רַב קָא אָתוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: שבתאי's conclusion from the story in step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: People without compassion must come from the ערב רב.

steps.title: Compassion is the sign of אברהם's children
steps.stepSummary: From the פסוק 'ונתן לך רחמים ורחמך' we learn that whoever has compassion on people is from אברהם's children, and whoever does not, is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And He will give you compassion and have compassion on you.' Anyone who has compassion on people, it is known that he is from the children of אברהם our father. And anyone who does not have compassion on people, it is known that he is not from the children of אברהם our father.
steps.whatsHappening: A פסוק is brought to support the claim that people without compassion are not אברהם's children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק connects the gift of compassion to the promise made to the fathers. So having compassion is a sign that someone belongs to אברהם's family. The rich Babylonians showed no compassion, which explains why שבתאי said they come from the ערב רב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is known, it is clear

steps.whatToRemember: Having compassion on others is the sign of being a true child of אברהם. Refusing even basic help to someone in need is the opposite.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And He will give you compassion, and have compassion on you,'
phrases.notes: דברים 13:18

phrases.english: anyone who has compassion on people —

phrases.aramaic: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁהוּא מִזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ,
phrases.english: it is known that he is from the children of Avraham our father,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מִי שֶׁאֵינוֹ מְרַחֵם עַל הַבְּרִיּוֹת —
phrases.english: and anyone who does not have compassion on people —

phrases.aramaic: בְּיָדוּעַ שֶׁאֵינוֹ מִזַּרְעוֹ שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ.
phrases.english: it is known that he is not from the children of Avraham our father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for שבתאי's claim in step 11
steps.raayaObject: The claim that people without compassion are not אברהם's children

steps.title: Depending on others' tables makes the world dark
steps.stepSummary: רב נתן בר אבא says in the name of רב that whoever depends on other people's tables lives in a dark world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נתן בר אבא also said in the name of רב: Anyone who looks to other people's tables for his food, the world is dark for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more saying of רב נתן בר אבא in the name of רב. Someone who relies on other people to feed him feels the whole world is dark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the series of sayings by the same speaker. Steps 9-12 spoke about the rich people who refused to help. Now the focus turns to the person who has to ask for help and how bleak his life feels.

keyTerms.meaning: one who looks to or waits for (someone else's food)
the table of others, meaning their food or support

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Natan bar Abba said that Rav said:
Whoever looks to the table of others
the world is dark for him,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נָתָן בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another saying in the same series of sayings by רב נתן בר אבא in the name of רב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who depends on others for food experiences the world as dark.

steps.title: The פסוק about wandering for bread
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק from איוב supports the idea that one who wanders for bread lives in darkness.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'He wanders for bread, saying where is it? He knows that a day of darkness is ready at his hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a פסוק as the source for רב's statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes someone wandering around looking for bread. It ends with 'a day of darkness.' That matches רב's words that the world is dark for such a person.

phrases.english: as it is stated:
"He wanders for bread: where is it?
phrases.notes: איוב 15:23

phrases.aramaic: יָדַע כִּי נָכוֹן בְּיָדוֹ יוֹם חֹשֶׁךְ״.
phrases.english: He knows that a day of darkness is ready at his hand."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the saying in step 13
steps.raayaObject: רב's statement that the world is dark for one who depends on others

steps.title: רב חסדא: his life is not a life
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא adds that such a person's life is not really a life.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Even his life is not a life.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא goes one step further than רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said the world looks dark to this person. רב חסדא says more: his life itself does not count as real living.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Even his life is not a life.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stronger statement on top of רב's saying
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who depends on others' tables has a life that is not a life.

steps.title: A ברייתא: three whose lives are not lives
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists three people whose lives are not lives, and the first is the one who depends on someone else's table.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: There are three people whose lives are not lives. They are: one who looks to his friend's table, one whose wife rules over him, and one whose body is ruled by suffering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב חסדא's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the same phrase as רב חסדא, 'their lives are not lives.' It lists the one who depends on his friend's table first, so רב חסדא's statement has a source in a ברייתא. The ברייתא also adds two more cases.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Three, their lives are not lives,
and these are they:
one who looks to his friend's table,
and one whose wife rules over him,
and one whose body is ruled by suffering.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה חַיֵּיהֶן אֵינָם חַיִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's statement with a ברייתא that uses the same words
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's claim that the life of one who depends on others is not a life
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing three whose lives are not lives

steps.title: Some add one who has only one garment
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion in the ברייתא adds a fourth case: someone who owns only one garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: Also one who has only one garment.
steps.whatsHappening: Another opinion, the יש אומרים, adds a fourth person to the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These תנאים agree with the three cases and add one more. A person with only one garment also lives a life that is not a life. The next step explains why the first תנא did not count him.

phrases.english: And some say:

phrases.aramaic: אַף מִי שֶׁאֵין לוֹ אֶלָּא חָלוּק אֶחָד.
phrases.english: Also one who has only one garment.
phrases.notes: With nothing to change into, he can't keep it clean, so it gets dirty and full of bugs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion inside the same ברייתא that widens the list
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who has only one garment is also among those whose lives are not lives.

steps.title: Why the first תנא leaves out the one-garment case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the תנא קמא holds this person can check his clothes, so his suffering is not that bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא holds: It is possible for him to check his clothes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why didn't the first תנא count the man with one garment? He can check his clothes and clean out the bugs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both opinions agree that a dirty single garment causes misery. They disagree about whether the problem can be fixed. The תנא קמא says he can search and clean his clothes, so his life still counts as a life.

keyTerms.meaning: the first תנא, whose opinion is stated first

phrases.english: And the first Tanna holds:
phrases.notes: This is the תנא who listed only three, without the one-garment case.

phrases.english: It is possible for him to examine his clothes.
phrases.notes: By checking his clothes he can get rid of the bugs, so his suffering can be fixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the first opinion did not include the case added in step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reason behind a תנא's position
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have thought the תנא קמא disagrees that one garment causes suffering.
steps.terutzMaskana: He agrees it causes suffering, but holds it can be fixed by checking the clothes, so it does not make life 'not a life.'
steps.whatToRemember: Three lives are 'not lives': one who depends on others' tables, one ruled by his wife, and one ruled by suffering. The יש אומרים add one with a single garment. The תנא קמא leaves that out because he can check and clean his clothes.

steps.title: New משנה: no breaking earthenware or cutting paper
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that on יום טוב one may not break earthenware or cut paper to roast salted fish on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not break earthenware, and one may not cut paper in order to roast salted fish on it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and returns to the laws of יום טוב. It forbids breaking earthenware or cutting paper to use while roasting salted fish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pieces of clay or paper were put under the fish so it would not burn. Even though it is for cooking, the משנה forbids making these pieces on יום טוב.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One may not break earthenware,
and one may not cut paper
in order to roast salted fish on it.
phrases.notes: The piece of clay or paper goes under the fish so the fish doesn't burn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אגדה and starts a new משנה on יום טוב laws
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may not break earthenware or cut paper to roast salted fish on it.
steps.confusionAlert: This is about cooking on יום טוב, yet it is still forbidden. Making the pieces counts as preparing a tool, not as preparing the food itself.

steps.title: No sweeping the oven, but pressing down is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids sweeping out an oven or stove on יום טוב but allows pressing down what is inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not sweep out an oven or a stove, but one may press down.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with ovens. Sweeping them out is forbidden, but pressing down and flattening is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates two actions in the same oven. Sweeping things out is forbidden. Pressing down the dust and ashes is permitted so the oven can still be used.

phrases.english: And one may not sweep out an oven or a stove,
but one may press down.
phrases.notes: He means flattening the ashes and dust inside, without clearing them out.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין גּוֹרְפִין תַּנּוּר וְכִירַיִם, אֲבָל מְכַבְּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה with a rule about ovens
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may not sweep out an oven or stove, but one may press down its contents.
steps.whatToRemember: The new משנה lists things not allowed on יום טוב even for cooking: breaking clay, cutting paper for roasting, and sweeping out an oven. Pressing down inside the oven is allowed.

steps.title: No setting up barrels or propping a pot
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids arranging two barrels to hold a pot, and forbids propping a pot with a piece of wood or a door.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not bring two barrels together to rest a pot on them. You may not prop up a pot with a piece of wood, and the same goes for a door.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues its list of things you may not do on יום טוב, now dealing with setting up a pot for cooking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists these rulings without giving reasons. For the barrels, the גמרא explains later (step 34) that a pot resting across them makes a tent. Propping a pot with wood or a door is listed here as a separate rule.

keyTerms.meaning: bringing close together, setting side by side

phrases.english: And one may not bring two barrels together
phrases.notes: The idea is to light a fire in the gap between the barrels, so they work like a stove.

phrases.english: to set the pot on them,
and one may not prop up the pot with a piece of wood,
and likewise with a door.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of forbidden kitchen preparations on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On יום טוב one may not arrange barrels to hold a pot, nor prop a pot with wood or a door.

steps.title: Leading an animal with a stick
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids leading an animal with a stick on יום טוב, while רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: You may not lead an animal with a stick on יום טוב. רבי אלעזר son of רבי שמעון permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a final ruling about leading an animal with a stick, and records a disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The unnamed first opinion forbids using a stick to drive an animal on יום טוב. רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון disagrees and allows it. The משנה gives no reason here; it only records the two opinions.

phrases.english: And one may not lead the animal
with a stick on יום טוב,
and Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon permits it.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's list ends here: no barrels as a stove, no propping a pot, and a מחלוקת about leading an animal with a stick.
steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין מַנְהִיגִין אֶת הַבְּהֵמָה בַּמַּקֵּל בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the last ruling of the משנה, this time with a disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא forbids leading an animal with a stick on יום טוב; רבי אלעזר ברבי שמעון permits.

steps.title: Why breaking earthenware is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why one may not break earthenware or cut paper to roast fish, and answers that this counts as making a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because he is making a usable utensil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and goes back to the first ruling of the משנה (breaking earthenware and cutting paper). It asks for the reason and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking off a piece of clay or cutting paper to the right size creates a new tool for roasting. Making a usable vessel is forbidden on יום טוב, even when it is for food.
steps.confusionAlert: This question does not go back to the last line of the משנה (leading an animal). It goes back to the first ruling, about breaking earthenware and cutting paper.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 19: breaking a piece of clay or cutting paper to roast salted fish on.

phrases.english: Because he is making a vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מְתַקֵּן מָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא opens by explaining the משנה's first ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for forbidding breaking earthenware or cutting paper on יום טוב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It counts as making a vessel, which is forbidden on יום טוב.

steps.title: Sweeping the oven is allowed if baking needs it
steps.stepSummary: רב חייא בר יוסף teaches a ברייתא: if baking is impossible without sweeping the oven, sweeping is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One may not sweep an oven or stove.' רב חייא בר יוסף taught in front of רב נחמן: If it is impossible to bake unless one sweeps it, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on sweeping an oven, then brings a teaching that limits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's ban covers sweeping that is not really needed. When baking cannot happen at all without sweeping, the sweeping becomes part of preparing food and is allowed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the key rule for the rest of the section: oven work that is truly needed for cooking can be allowed.

phrases.english: And one may not sweep out an oven or stove.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה we saw in step 20.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן:
phrases.english: Rav Ḥiyya bar Yosef taught before Rav Naḥman:
And if it is impossible to bake
unless one sweeps it out, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sweeping an oven on יום טוב is permitted when baking is impossible otherwise.

steps.title: רבי חייא hints to his wife to clear the oven
steps.stepSummary: A brick piece fell into the oven of רבי חייא's wife on יום טוב, and he hinted that she could remove it by saying he wanted good bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: A piece of brick fell into the oven of רבי חייא's wife on יום טוב. רבי חייא said to her: 'Look, I want really good bread.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story that shows the rule from the ברייתא being used in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a brick in the oven, good bread is impossible. By saying he wants good bread, רבי חייא makes the removal 'needed for baking,' so it becomes permitted under the ברייתא's rule.

phrases.english: The wife of Rabbi Ḥiyya:

phrases.aramaic: נְפַל לַהּ אֲרִיחָא בְּתַנּוּרָא בְּיוֹמָא טָבָא,
phrases.english: a piece of brick fell into her oven on יום טוב,
Rabbi Ḥiyya said to her: See,
I want good-quality bread.
phrases.notes: He is hinting: good bread can't be baked with a brick in there, so go ahead and take it out.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבֵיתְהוּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא נְפַל לַהּ אֲרִיחָא בְּתַנּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the ברייתא's rule put into practice.
steps.raayaObject: Clearing the oven is allowed when it is needed for proper baking.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי חייא's wife and the brick in the oven.

steps.title: רבא tells his attendant not to burn the duck
steps.stepSummary: רבא told his attendant to roast a duck without burning it, quietly allowing him to clean the oven for that purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to his attendant: 'Roast a duck for me, and be careful it doesn't get burnt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second story with the same idea as the story of רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Roasting without burning needs a clean oven. By asking for an unburnt duck, רבא makes the cleaning needed for the food, so it fits the ברייתא's rule.

phrases.english: Rava said to his attendant:
Roast a duck for me,
and be careful not to singe it.

steps.whatToRemember: Clearing out an oven on יום טוב is fine when it is truly needed so the food comes out properly.
steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְשַׁמָּעֵיהּ טְוִי לִי בַּר אֲווֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel story backing up the same rule.
steps.raayaObject: Preparing the oven is allowed when it is needed for the food to come out properly.

steps.title: Did רב אשי seal his oven on יום טוב?
steps.stepSummary: רבינא tells רב אשי he heard that רב אשי's oven was plastered shut on יום טוב, which needs an explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: רב אחא from Hutzal told us that people plaster your oven shut for you on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא reports something surprising about רב אשי's practice. This sets up a question that רב אשי answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sealing an oven usually means mixing mud with water, which looks like forbidden kneading. רבינא wants to know how this was allowed.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
Rav Aḥa from Hutzal told us

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר שָׁרְקִין לֵיהּ תַּנּוּרָא בְּיוֹמָא טָבָא.
phrases.english: that for the master, they plaster the oven on יום טוב.
phrases.notes: They seal the oven's opening with mud so the food cooks well inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר לַן רַב אַחָא מֵהוּצָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from clearing an oven to sealing an oven on יום טוב.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How sealing an oven with mud on יום טוב is permitted, since it seems to involve kneading.

steps.title: Using ready-made riverbank mud
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that they use mud from the bank of the פרת, which is already mixed, so no kneading is done.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: We rely on the mud of the bank of the Euphrates.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא's question about sealing the oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mud from the riverbank is already soft and mixed by nature. Using it means nobody kneads anything on יום טוב, so the problem goes away.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנַן אַרַקְתָּא דִפְרָת סָמְכִינַן,
phrases.english: He said to him: We rely on the mud of the bank of the Euphrates.
phrases.notes: That mud is already soft and ready to use, so no one has to mix it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mud used was already naturally mixed riverbank mud, so no kneading took place.

steps.title: Only if the mud was set aside the day before
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא limits רב אשי's answer: the mud may be used only if it was set aside before יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this applies only when he marked it off the day before.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a condition to רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even ready-made mud is not normally meant for use, so it would be off-limits on יום טוב. It may be used only if someone set it aside for this purpose before יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: he marked it off, set it aside

phrases.english: And this applies only when he marked it off the day before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רב אשי's permission.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Riverbank mud may be used to seal an oven on יום טוב only if it was set aside before יום טוב.

steps.title: Ashes are permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבינא rules that sealing the oven with ashes is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: And ashes are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא closes the section with one more allowed option for sealing an oven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ashes are listed as simply permitted, without the conditions given for riverbank mud. This gives an easy option for sealing an oven on יום טוב.
steps.whatToRemember: An oven may be sealed on יום טוב with ready-made riverbank mud set aside the day before, and ashes are permitted.

phrases.english: Ravina said: And ashes are permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final permitted material for sealing the oven.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Using ashes to seal an oven on יום טוב is permitted.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about barrels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה that one may not draw two barrels together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: One may not draw two barrels together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to start a new discussion. This is a setup line that prepares for the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה forbids pushing two barrels together so a pot can rest on top. The גמרא brings it up now because a related ruling, and a challenge built on this line, are about to follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Drawing together, placing side by side

phrases.english: And one may not draw two barrels together.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה. The full line adds "to rest a pot on them," as the next steps show.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the oven-sealing discussion to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may not draw two barrels together on יום טוב to rest a pot on them.

steps.title: Bathroom stones may be arranged on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the stones of an outhouse may be set in place on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: The stones of a bathroom may be arranged on יום טוב.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives a ruling: you may set up the stones used in an outhouse on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Setting stones into place can look like building. Even so, רב נחמן allows it here, which raises the question of how this fits with the barrels in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: To arrange them, to set them in place

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Stones of a bathroom,
it is permitted to arrange them on יום טוב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling that seems to clash with the משנה just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bathroom stones may be arranged on יום טוב.

steps.title: Challenge from the barrels
steps.stepSummary: רבה challenges רב נחמן from the משנה, which forbids drawing barrels together to rest a pot on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה challenged רב נחמן: But we learned that one may not draw two barrels together to place a pot on them!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks רב נחמן's ruling using the משנה about the barrels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If arranging two barrels counts as forbidden building, then arranging bathroom stones should be forbidden too. The two cases look the same, so רבה asks why רב נחמן permits the stones.

keyTerms.meaning: To set a pot on the fire or on a support

phrases.english: Rabba challenged Rav Nachman:
One may not draw two barrels together
to place the pot on them!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's ruling from step 32.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's permission to arrange bathroom stones
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Arranging barrels is forbidden as building, so arranging stones should be forbidden too.

steps.title: Barrels are different because they make a tent
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the barrels are forbidden because placing a pot over them forms a tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: It is different there, because one makes a tent.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן explains why the barrels are different from the bathroom stones.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem with the barrels is not that they are moved together. The problem is that a pot resting across them covers an empty space, which forms a tent. Bathroom stones make no tent, so they are allowed.

phrases.english: He said to him: It is different there,
because one makes a tent.
phrases.notes: The pot lies across both barrels with open space underneath, so it forms a little roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any arranging of objects counts as forbidden building.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only making a tent (a covering over open space) is forbidden, so the stones are permitted.

steps.title: Then a solid bench should be allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבה זוטא asks רב אשי: by that logic, building a solid bench on יום טוב, which makes no tent, should be permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה זוטא said to רב אשי: If so, if one built a bench on יום טוב, which does not make a tent, would it also be permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה זוטא challenges the idea that only making a tent is forbidden, using a solid bench as an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the only problem is a tent, then building a solid bench, which has no open space under it, should be fine. That cannot be right, since it is clearly building, so the reasoning in step 34 seems too narrow.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so, according to this logic
So too, would you also say

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה זוּטָא, לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rabba the Younger said to Rav Ashi:

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה, בָּנָה אִצְטְבָא בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: But if so, if one built a bench on יום טוב,
where he does not make a tent,
phrases.notes: He means a solid bench with no open space underneath.

phrases.english: is it also permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning given in step 34.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that only making a tent is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A solid bench makes no tent, yet it is obviously building, so tent-making cannot be the only issue.

steps.title: Permanent vs. temporary building, and human dignity
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the Torah forbids permanent building, and the רבנן also banned temporary building, but they did not ban it for bathroom stones because of dignity.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, the Torah forbade permanent building and did not forbid temporary building. The רבנן made a decree against temporary building because of permanent building. But here, because of a person's dignity, the רבנן did not make the decree.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers by explaining the levels of the building prohibition and why the bathroom stones are an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bench is real building. The Torah itself forbids only permanent building, while the רבנן added a ban on temporary building so people would not come to build permanently. For bathroom stones, the רבנן chose not to apply their ban, out of respect for a person's dignity (כבוד הבריות).
steps.whatToRemember: The Torah forbids only permanent building. Temporary building is forbidden by the רבנן, but they left it permitted for bathroom stones because of human dignity.
steps.confusionAlert: Arranging bathroom stones still counts as temporary building. It is an exception where the רבנן did not apply their decree, not something outside the category of building.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key rule for building on יום טוב and שבת: the Torah forbids permanent building, the רבנן extend the ban to temporary building, and they sometimes waive it for human dignity.

phrases.english: He said to him: There,
phrases.notes: "There" means the case of the bench.

phrases.english: the Torah forbade permanent building,
temporary building the Torah did not forbid.
And the Sages decreed against temporary building
because of permanent building,
and here, because of his dignity,
the Sages did not decree regarding it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם, בִּנְיַן קֶבַע אָסְרָה תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה זוטא's challenge by redefining why the stones are permitted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the prohibition into a Torah level and a rabbinic level, with an exception for dignity
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only tent-making is forbidden, so any non-tent structure would be allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Any building is at least forbidden by the רבנן, but they did not apply that ban to bathroom stones because of human dignity.

steps.title: Stacking a bonfire: top-down vs. bottom-up
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rules that a bonfire arranged from top to bottom is permitted, but from bottom to top is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: With this bonfire, arranging it from above to below is permitted. From below to above is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives a new ruling about how wood may be stacked for a fire on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stacking from the bottom up is the normal way of building, so it counts as building and is forbidden. Stacking from the top down, holding the upper pieces and then placing supports under them, is not the normal way to build, so it is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A bonfire, a pile of wood for a fire

steps.whatToRemember: Doing something in an unusual way (top-down) takes it out of the forbidden building pattern.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This bonfire,
from above to below, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: You hold the top pieces up first and then slip the bottom pieces underneath.

phrases.english: From below to above, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling that continues the theme of what counts as building on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Arranging a bonfire from the top down is permitted; from the bottom up is forbidden.
